title: L3Harris Awarded Joint Capability Group Contract for Advanced Capability System Implementation
summary: L3Harris Technologies has received a contract from the Australian Department of Defence’s Joint Capability Group to deliver an advanced, platform-agnostic capability with potential applications across land, air and maritime domains.
body_markdown:
L3Harris Technologies has received a contract from the Australian Department of Defence’s Joint Capability Group to deliver an advanced, platform-agnostic capability with potential applications across land, air and maritime domains.


Awarded following a competitive tender process, the contract will be executed by L3Harris Space and Airborne Systems Australia from its Electronic Warfare Centre of Excellence in Eight-Mile Plains, Queensland, and will support Australia’s integrated force. The contract is valued at approximately $28 million.


> “This award reflects Defence’s confidence in our Australian team’s ability to implement sophisticated, operationally relevant capability,” said Ian Charles, Managing Director, L3Harris Space and Airborne Systems Australia Pty Ltd. “Our work builds on years of support out of L3Harris in Queensland for Australia’s Joint Force, and we remain firmly focused on delivering an effective and dependable system for Defence.”


The Brisbane facility specialises in the design, manufacture, integration and sustainment of high-reliability electronic warfare components and subsystems that detect, guide and protect in extreme operating environments. The facility is an established exporter to global defence prime contractors and a trusted partner of the Australian Department of Defence.


The program will draw on multidisciplinary engineering, systems integration and program-delivery expertise within L3Harris’ Australian business.


> “This contract will support the delivery of an advanced capability for Australia’s integrated force,” said Nelson Bates, Assistant Secretary, Joint Capabilities Group, Australian Department of Defence. “Working with Australian industry helps Defence draw on specialised engineering and systems-integration expertise as we continue to strengthen the capabilities available to the Australian Defence Force.”


The capabilities offered by L3Harris’ Electronic Warfare Centre of Excellence are complemented by the company’s Indo-Pacific Regional Support Centre in Brisbane, which serves as a key sustainment hub for Australia and regional partners. L3Harris continues to demonstrate its investment in advanced Australian sovereign program delivery in support of the 2026 National Defence Strategy.
